vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cn-holiday-checker
Version: 1.0.1

The skill is a legitimate utility for checking Chinese holiday and work-shift schedules. It downloads calendar data from reputable sources (Apple iCloud and a known GitHub repository) and parses it using standard libraries (requests, icalendar) without any signs of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions match its description: it downloads public .ics calendar files (configurable), reads them, and decides workdays; nothing requests unrelated credentials or hidden endpoints.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Chinese holiday lookup + workday determination) align with included files: a downloader that fetches an .ics and a checker that parses it. The declared config.json URLs point to plausible holiday sources (iCloud public holidays and a GitHub mirror). One minor mismatch: SKILL.md says config.json "stores environment variables," but it actually stores URLs in JSON — functionally acceptable but wording is inaccurate.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running download_ics.py to refresh and holiday_checker.py to query dates; it suggests using cron for periodic updates but does not instruct reading other system files or credentials. The runtime scripts only read config.json and the downloaded data file and do not exfiltrate data or contact unexpected endpoints beyond the configured URLs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only with two small scripts included. No external installer or downloaded code at install time. Runtime download_ics.py fetches remote .ics files from the URLs in config.json, which is expected behavior for keeping calendar data fresh.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no credentials or environment variables. Configuration is done via config.json (PRIMARY_URL / BACKUP_URL). This is proportional to the skill's purpose. Note: because the downloader uses whatever URL is present in config.json, pointing that file at an untrusted URL would cause the skill to fetch arbitrary content — not a vulnerability in the skill itself but a configuration risk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or modify system configuration. It only reads/writes within its project tree (reads config.json, writes data/cn_zh.ics). SKILL.md suggests the user set up a cron job, but the skill does not create persistent system services itself.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and limited in scope, but review a few practical points before installing: (1) Ensure the project has a local data/ directory (download_ics.py writes data/cn_zh.ics and will error if the directory is missing). (2) Inspect and, if desired, change PRIMARY_URL/BACKUP_URL in config.json — the downloader will fetch whatever URL you configure, so avoid pointing it to untrusted hosts. (3) SKILL.md's wording about "environment variables" is misleading; configuration is via the JSON file. (4) If you plan to automate updates with cron, ensure the scheduled job runs in a controlled environment (permissions and network access) you trust. Overall, no credentials are requested and no hidden network endpoints were found.
